one_line: Mughal prince and scholar translating Sanskrit Upanishads into Persian in the 1650s.

appearance.age_look: Mid-30s, tall and slim with a slightly scholarly posture but a quietly regal bearing.
appearance.face: Oval face with a straight nose, warm light-brown complexion, neatly trimmed black mustache and short pointed beard, thoughtful dark eyes with a calm, introspective default expression.
appearance.hair: Black hair worn medium length but mostly hidden under a pale cream Mughal turban wrapped flat and low, with a narrow green cloth band and a small central jeweled turban ornament in gold and red.
appearance.costume: A knee-length fine cotton jama in soft light-cream with long overlapping front panels tied to the left, subtly patterned with very thin gold-beige vertical stripes, worn over a plain white under-tunic; a deep forest-green silk patka (waist sash) tied firmly at the waist with its ends hanging slightly to the left, and straight, narrow white churidar trousers gathered at the ankles; on the feet, simple brown leather Moorish-style shoes with slightly upturned toes; over one shoulder, a lightweight pale-blue shawl with a slim gold border, draped so it falls diagonally across his torso to the opposite hip, hinting at his scholarly, courtly role in Banaras, Agra and Delhi.
appearance.signature: A well-used but elegant palm-leaf–colored Persian manuscript volume held in one hand—with visible cream pages edged in gold and a dark reddish-brown leather cover—while a simple, sheathed Mughal dagger with a plain bone or ivory-colored hilt sits tucked modestly into his green waist sash, showing both his princely rank and his life as a translator of the Upanishads.

ref_desc: Dara Shukoh is a tall, slim Mughal prince in a light-cream striped jama, white churidar, forest-green waist sash, pale-blue shawl, cream turban with a small gold-red ornament, carrying a reddish-brown Persian manuscript and a plain-hilted dagger at his sash.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of Dara Shukoh as a Mughal prince-scholar in 1650s North India: a tall, slim man in his mid-30s with an oval face, light-brown complexion, thoughtful dark eyes, a neatly trimmed black mustache and small pointed beard, and medium black hair mostly hidden under a pale cream flat-wrapped turban banded with a narrow green strip and a small central gold-and-red jewel ornament. Dress him in a knee-length fine cotton jama in soft light-cream with subtle thin gold-beige vertical stripes, the overlapping front panels tied to the left, over a plain white under-tunic, with straight white churidar trousers gathered at the ankles and simple brown leather shoes with slightly upturned toes. Add a deep forest-green silk patka (waist sash) tied firmly, its ends hanging a bit to the left, and drape a lightweight pale-blue shawl with a slim gold border over one shoulder so it crosses diagonally over his torso. In his right hand, place a well-used yet elegant Persian manuscript volume with a dark reddish-brown leather cover and cream pages edged in gold, and show a simple sheathed Mughal dagger with a plain bone or ivory-colored hilt tucked modestly into his green sash; keep his default expression calm and introspective, with dignified, scholarly energy, using a palette of light cream, forest green, pale blue, white and brown leather tones.
